year_launched.note: ANCC nurse executive credentialing has existed since the 1990s but a specific NE-BC launch year was not located on the issuing body page during this run.

eligibility.value: Hold a current, active U.S. RN license (or legally recognized equivalent in another country); a bachelor's or higher degree in nursing; the equivalent of 2 years full-time practice as an RN; a minimum of 2,000 hours of nursing administration practice within the last 3 years; and 30 hours of continuing education in nursing administration within the last 3 years.

exam_format.value: Computer-based at Prometric test centers (and remote-proctored option per ANCC). Competency-based, multiple-choice. 175 items total (150 scored + 25 pretest), 3.5-hour time limit.
exam_format.note: Item count and time confirmed against certs.js (175 questions). One secondary source (mometrix) lists 150/3hr; the ANCC handbook value 175/3.5hr is treated as canonical.

passing_score.value: Scaled score of 350 on a 0-500 scale

fee_retake.note: Retake allowed no sooner than 60 days after a failed attempt.

pass_rate_latest.value: 66% (most recently reported pass rate per ANCC certification data)
pass_rate_latest.note: Total NE-BC credential holders reported at 9,156 as of the same data release.

renewal.value: 5-year cycle. Renew by completing 75 hours of continuing education in nurse executive practice plus one additional professional development category, or by retaking the certification exam.

value.disambiguation: Nurse Executive Advanced - Board Certified, also from ANCC, is the system or enterprise-level credential and requires a master's degree plus broader executive scope. NE-BC targets unit, team, service-line, department, or program leaders.

Certified in Executive Nursing Practice from AONL is a competing executive credential aimed at nurse leaders at the executive level; NE-BC is ANCC's parallel offering for first-line and middle nurse leaders.

recent_changes.value: ANCC Certification Renewal Requirements handbook effective September 10, 2025 governs the current renewal cycle.

blueprint.note: ANCC publishes the Test Content Outline as a downloadable PDF; specific 2025-2026 domain weights were not extracted during this run. Secondary sources describe the major content areas as Human Resource Management, Quality and Safety, Business Management, and Health Care Delivery.

discrepancies.resolution: Use 175 per ANCC's published handbook and internal certs.js data.
